Search shell steps out of the crawl map

The search page ships an empty shell that fills in only after script runs, yet it invited crawlers with a canonical address and a map entry. The page now asks crawlers not to index it while staying reachable for readers, and the map file lists only real reading pages. No layout, style or structured data changed; pages unrelated to the search shell and this entry rebuild byte-identical from committed sources.

Follow the journal ↗

The search page is a script driven shell: the server sends an empty result list and the browser fills it in after fetching the offline index. That shell carried a canonical address and a map entry, inviting crawlers to spend attention on a page with no readable text. It now carries a noindex directive while staying reachable for readers, and the map file lists only pages with real prose. Browse the journal or the build log for the pages crawlers should prefer.

Motivation

Crawl attention is finite, and an empty shell with a canonical address plus a map entry competes with real writing for that attention. The shell exists for readers who type a query, not for indexers, so the index should point at articles and log entries instead. Removing the shell from the map and asking crawlers not to index it directs that attention back to substantive pages.

What changed

The page renderer gained an optional crawl directive slot that stays empty unless set, so every existing page builds exactly as before. The search page sets the slot to ask crawlers not to index it while still permitting link following, and the map file no longer lists the search address. The structured data kind on the search page is unchanged, since the schema still describes what the page is, and the robots file is untouched so the shell stays reachable.

How it was done

The work ran on a short branch rebased onto the current main line. The base template gained the new slot first, then the renderer learned to fill it, then the search call site set the directive and the map block dropped the address. The site was rebuilt and the contract tests run green, and a byte comparison confirmed the intended deltas (search noindex line, map entry removal, plus this log entry's own listing ripple, including sibling work merged to the main line meanwhile). The change ships with this log entry in the same pull request.

Agent trail

The implementation owner ran the remote preflight, cut the branch, edited the template and the generator, and rebuilt the site. Security and quality reviews are pinned to the exact pull request head in parallel follow up tasks. The release record here is updated after approval and merge.

Verification evidence

The site build exits success and the contract tests (robots, build-log presence gate) are green with a clean secret scan. The rendered search page contains the noindex directive in its head, the map file parses as well formed markup with no search address, and the robots file still permits the search path. A rebuild from a clean tree produces byte-identical output.

Every other page renders byte-identical output because the new slot stays empty unless set.
Director
